title: Fragmented response recovery and tool sandboxing (PRD notes)
content:
Summary:
This doc sketches a pragmatic PRD for handling fragmented/partial streamed responses while enabling robust tool-calling and a client-local "sandbox" mode for deterministic replay and safety checks. We focus on: resumable partial responses, compact structured-output deltas, idempotent action tokens for tool-calls, and lightweight local sandbox simulation in SDKs to improve developer confidence and reduce production surprises.

Motivation / problem statement:
Teams building integrations with streamed model output and external tool invocation run into three recurring problems: 1) network or client interruptions cause partial outputs that are hard to reconcile deterministically; 2) tool-calls executed mid-stream create side-effects that are difficult to recover from if a request is retried or resumed; 3) developer uptake is slowed because SDKs lack a cheap local sandbox workflow to validate structured outputs and tool-call contracts before hitting production.

Goals (90-day):
- Define a minimal streaming handshake and tokenized recovery protocol so clients can resume fragments without double-executing external actions.
- Add a compact "delta-of-structures" schema to represent partial structured output (JSON diffs, typed frames) with ordering metadata.
- Introduce an idempotent action token and commit/abort semantics for tool-calls.
- Deliver an SDK feature (local sandbox mode) that can simulate tool-call responses and validate structured-output contracts during dev-time.
- Instrument telemetry for partial-response frequency, resumed-sessions, and aborted vs committed tool invocations.

Non-goals:
- Full transactional guarantees across heterogeneous external systems (we will provide guardrails and tokens, not distributed transactions).
- Large breaking changes to existing streaming endpoints; aim for opt-in extension fields.

API surface (high level):
- StreamFrame: {frame_id, session_id, seq, type: [text|delta|action|meta], payload: string, prev_hash?}  (payload is the stringified JSON or text chunk).
- ActionProposal: {action_id, action_token, action_spec, dry_run} returned as a frame type "action".
- ActionCommit / ActionAbort: explicit client-side frames or POST endpoint that binds action_token -> final outcome.
- ResumeRequest: client posts resume metadata (session_id, last_seq_received) and receives an ordered stream starting from next seq and a reconciliation diff.

SDK ergonomics (developer experience):
- Default client behavior: stateless streaming as today. Opt-in via header "Prefer: session-resume=v1" to enable tokenized behavior.
- High-level SDK primitives: startSession(), onFrame(cb), proposeAction(spec), commitAction(action_token, result), abortAction(action_token).
- Local sandbox: lightweight mode that stubs proposeAction responses using user-provided connectors or canned policies. The sandbox validates structured output shape and highlights potential mismatches before network calls.
- Safety-first defaults: proposeAction returns a synthetic action_token with conservative TTL; SDK will prevent auto-commit without explicit commitAction call in sandbox mode.

Streaming handshake & recovery protocol (sketch):
1) Session start returns session_id and streaming seed hash. Frames carry an increasing seq number and prev_hash (optional) to detect divergence.
2) For frames that represent tool-call proposals, server emits an "action" frame with an action_token and an action_spec describing preconditions. No side effects occur until the client issues commitAction.
3) If a client disconnects, it can request ResumeRequest(session_id, last_seq). Server returns any frames after last_seq plus a reconciliation delta (if server advanced state while client was offline).
4) CommitAction binds the action_token on the server; server-side checks token validity and idempotency to avoid duplicate side-effects. AbortAction invalidates token.

Tool sandboxing and local simulation:
- SDKs provide a developer-mode flag that routes proposeAction to a sandbox layer. Sandbox behavior options: canned responses, parametrized mockers, or exec through a local shim of the customer connector.
- A sandbox log records action_proposals and simulated outcomes to a replayable artifact (small JSONL file) that can be attached to bug reports or e2e test artifacts.
- The sandbox will run a lightweight static validator against action_spec and the structured-output schema and warn on mismatches.

Structured output delta protocol (compactness & reconciliation):
- Use small typed-change frames instead of full JSON re-sends: op: [add|remove|replace], path: JSON-pointer, value. Each delta frame references seq base so clients can apply in-order or request full state if they miss too many frames.
- To reduce bandwidth, allow server-side summarized checkouts: every N frames include a snapshot hash and an optional snapshot payload on request.

Observability & telemetry:
Capture the following signals as first-class metrics:
- partial_frame_rate (fraction of sessions with incomplete final frame on disconnect)
- resume_success_rate and avg_resume_delta_size
- action_proposals_per_session, action_commit_rate, action_abort_rate, action_duplicate_rejects
- sandbox_usage_by_active_dev and sandbox_validation_warnings

Success metrics (30/90/180-day):
- 30d: SDK sandbox implemented in JS + Python with sample local connectors; telemetry enabled in prod for opt-in sessions.
- 90d: Resume protocol live as opt-in; resume_success_rate >= 95% for sessions with <= 5 missed frames. Action duplicate rejects < 0.5% of commits.
- 180d: Reduce customer-reported partial-response bugs by 60% in projects using the resume + sandbox flow.

Rollout plan (incremental):
- Alpha: internal teams + 2 partner customers. Feature disabled by default; opt-in header. Collect telemetry and iterate.
- Beta: broader public opt-in; SDKs created/updated and docs + migration guide supplied.
- GA: enable headers in console per-project toggles, provide migration checklist for enterprise Dedicated/Private customers.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- TTL and storage: how long to keep unresolved action_tokens server-side (cost vs developer UX)? Suggest 24 hours default with configurable tenant policy.
- Failure semantics: what happens if commitAction arrives but the server lost the session snapshot? Need idempotent backend checks and conservative "unknown" result handling.
- Complexity vs ergonomics: minimize mandatory API steps; prefer server-side safeguards so developers are not burdened with low-level reconciliation.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: increased API surface adds complexity for basic streaming users. Mitigation: make tokenized behavior opt-in and keep simple text frames unchanged.
- Risk: mis-simulated sandbox leads to false confidence. Mitigation: provide clear annotations in sandbox artifacts and require explicit QA sign-off before cutting over.

Next steps / immediate todo:
- Spike: implement server-side action_token lifecycle and resume endpoint prototype (eng-serving-runtime + platform-engineering) (2 wks).
- SDKs: add sandbox layer and primitives in JS + Python; include a sample connector shim (3 wks).
- UX: draft console toggle UX and project-level opt-in docs (1 wk).
- Telemetry: instrument resume and action metrics in the console + pipeline (2 wks).

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conservative and opt-in. Feedback wanted on token TTL, snapshot cadence (every N frames), and recommended default sandbox policies.

Attachments (examples to produce during spike):
- minimal Wire Protocol spec (text), sample SDK calls (JS pseudocode), sandbox JSONL sample, telemetry dashboard mockups.
